data.name: Paulos
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'paulos', meaning 'small' or 'humble'. In the New Testament, St. Paul (originally named Saul) adopted this name after his conversion to Christianity. His letters to the Corinthians and others form a significant portion of the New Testament.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes humility and devotion to God.
data.numerology_meaning: Represents new beginnings and the ability to create one's own reality.

in_hebrew.name: פאולוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פאולוס מקורו ביוונית ופירושו קטן או צנוע, הוא היה אחד מהשליחים המרכזיים של ישו והוא ידוע בשליחת המכתבים שלו לנוצרים הראשונים, כמו גם בשליחתו לגויים. השם משמש כזכר לאחד מהאישים המשפיעים ביותר על הנצרות.

in_greek.name: Παῦλος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Παῦλος εἰς τὸ Ἑλληνιστὶ ὀνομάζεται, καὶ σημαίνει «ὁ μικρός» ἤ «ὁ ταπεινός». Ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἦν ἕνας τῶν κύριων ἀποστόλων τοῦ ΙἸησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ γνωρίζουμε τὸ έργο του ἀπὸ τὶς ἐπιστολές του πρὸς τοὺς πρώτους Χριστιανούς, καθὼς καὶ ἀπὸ τὴν κήρυξή του εἰς τοὺς ἐθνικούς. Τὸ ὄνομα Παῦλος εἶναι ἕνα ἀπὸ τὰ πιὸ ἐπιρρεπή οὐσιαστικά ὀνόματα στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη.

in_latin.name: Paulos
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Paulus a Graeco derivatum est et interpretatur 'parvus' vel 'modicus' sive 'humilis'. Paulus apostolus, unus ex primis Christi discipulis, fuit vir maximus et celeberrimus in Ecclesia primitiva. Epistolae eius ad primi Christianos datae et labores eius pro Christo evangelizando inter nationes sunt valde notae. Nomen igitur Pauli est nomen sanctum et insignis momenti in traditione Christiana.

in_english.name: Paulos
in_english.long_meaning: The name Paulos originates from the Greek word 'Παῦλος' (Paulos), meaning 'small,' 'humble,' or 'modest.' It is derived from the Latin 'Paulus,' which shares the same meaning. In Christian tradition, Paulos (or Paul) is a significant name due to Saint Paul, one of Jesus Christ's apostles, who played a crucial role in spreading Christianity. The name symbolizes humility and modesty, reflecting the apostle's initial name, Saul of Tarsus, who later became known as Paul. This name has been widely used across various Christian cultures and continues to be popular among Christian families.

biblical_reference.note: The name Paulos is directly mentioned in the New Testament, particularly in the Acts of the Apostles and in the Epistles of Paul.

saint_reference.note: Saint Paul, formerly known as Saul of Tarsus, was one of the most important figures in the early Christian Church, known for his missionary journeys and his letters to early Christian communities.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Paulos' has been popular in the Christian world due to its biblical significance through St. Paul. It is commonly found among people of Christian faith and is used in various Western and Eastern Christian traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Paulos' embodies the virtue of humility and smallness. Following the example set by St. Paul, it serves as a reminder to keep a humble and servant-like attitude, putting others before oneself and striving towards spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Paul of Tarsus, also known as St. Paul, was a key figure in the spread of Christianity in the 1st century AD. He was born in Tarsus, Cilicia (modern-day Turkey), and was a devout Pharisee before his conversion to Christianity around AD 33-35. He became a missionary and traveler, spreading the gospel to Greece, Macedonia, and Asia Minor, among other places.
historical_references.context: Early Christianity and spread of the gospel in the Roman Empire

historical_references.reference: Paul of Constantinople, also known as Paul the Silentarian, was a 4th-century bishop of Constantinople. He was a prominent theologian and participated in the First Council of Constantinople in 330 AD, where he defended the orthodox doctrine against Arianism. He is also known for his opposition to Nestorianism and his contribution to the development of the Trinitarian doctrine.
historical_references.context: Early Christian theology and the development of the Trinity doctrine in the Eastern Roman Empire

In Christian tradition, St. Paul, who was once Saul, underwent a profound transformation, renouncing his pride and embracing humility.
